Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

trial noun

in a court of law

also on trial, stand trial, put on trial, bring to trial, go on trial

classical

Cic. Caec. 6
Traupman 197

jūdicium, jūdiciī n.

noun, second declension

a trial

To bring someone to trial, in jūdicium addūcere; to be on trial for something, jūdicium dē aliquā rē subīre (Traupman 197); to stand trial, defending oneself, causam dīcere.

Examples

  • omnia jūdicia aut distrahendārum contrōversiārum aut pūniendōrum maleficiōrum causā reperta sunt

    all trials were devised either to settle disputes or to punish crimesCic. Caec. 6

  • Jūdicium nōtum fīēbat.

    A famous trial was being held.Traupman 190

Other words

  • quaestiō, quaestiōnis f. — a criminal trial; the standing court that tried one kind of crime

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fin. 2.54: cum praetor quaestiōnem inter sīcāriōs exercuisset (Lewis & Short); Traupman 197

    Held before a praetor and a jury; to conduct a trial, quaestiōnem exercēre (Traupman 197).

See also court, case, witness, lawyer, guilty, innocent, charge.

SourcesLewis & Short: judicium · Lewis & Short: quaestio
